text:
alexa: heads-up: saw a spike in p95/p99 for chat routes this morning and traced it to a collapse in prefix cache hit-rate for RAG-ish prompts. hit-rate went from ~48% -> ~6% after yesterday's keying PR. p99 latency up ~12-18% depending on model.

mike: ugh. which keying change exactly? the dedupe normalization?

alexa: mike yep.  #PR 4387 changed prefix fingerprint to include conversation metadata (turn IDs) to fix collision bug. we forgot to stable-hash some optional fields, so small variations exploded cardinality.

sara: can you paste a quick sample of before/after keys?

alexa: pasted below (sanitized):
```
// before: joined entity shingle + prompt-trim
pref_abc123::user:what is the price of widget
context:product#sku:9876

// after: naive json stringify of metadata
pref_a1b2c3::{"turn_id":0,"user":"what is the price of widget","meta":{"sku":9876}}
```

mike: yeah that will explode. small user-side noise -> new keys.

jia: quick question: are we seeing the regression only for chat/RAG or also plain completions?

alexa: mostly chat+RAG where we attach embeddings/structured metadata. completions stable. also worse for long-context because we store more prefix fragments.

sara: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) revert PR to restore old fingerprinting 2) implement a "soft-match" fallback where we canonicalize non-essential fields 3) increase TTL to allow background compaction 4) run offline dedupe job to collapse high-cardinality keys.

mike: I like soft-match. concrete: compute two fingerprints: strong and compact. lookup strong first, if miss, lookup compact which strips optional fields and normalizes numbers/IDs to buckets. Keep both in cache.

jia: brief perf note: extra lookup adds ~0.6ms median but saves miss penalty of ~25-40ms. for our p99 that matters. we should simulate with load replay.

alexa: ran a replay on staging for soft-match approach (compact -> hashed by shingle level). hit-rate jumped to 42% and p99 dropped back ~9-11% vs baseline. attaching small summary: 
- baseline (pre-PR): hit 48%, p99 210ms
- post-PR: hit 6%, p99 270ms
- soft-match: hit 42%, p99 224ms

mike: nice. can we avoid double writes complexity? cache write path should write both keys atomically or write strong then async write compact.

sara: prefer async write for performance. write strong synchronously, enqueue compact key write. if compact write fails it's okay.

alexa: implemented async write in staging and ran canary for 15m on 2 instances. results look consistent with replay.

deploy-bot: canary deployed by alexa to staging/eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-17T14:22:11Z :rocket:

jia: follow-ups: we should add telemetry for high-cardinality prefixes (top-N entropy), plus a sampling histogram of metadata fields that cause splits. that will prevent this surprise.

mike: agreed. also add a lint rule in PR pipeline to warn when fingerprint includes unbounded fields (raw UUID, timestamps, free-text).

alexa: I'll open follow-up PRs: one for soft-match + async write, one for telemetry, one for pipeline lint. will coordinate rollout plan: canary -> 10% prod -> 100% over 6h with auto-rollback on >5% p99 regression.

sara: timeline?

alexa: aiming for hotfix today. canary pass expected in 1-2h, then gradual rollout.

mike: thanks. one more ask: consider kernel selection impact — compact keys change request size distribution (more cache hits => fewer KV cache loads) so we may need to retune batching heuristics in the runtime for the new hit patterns. I'll run a microbenchmark for batch size vs latency under the soft-match hit-rate.

jia: ping me when benchmark results are in and I'll adjust autoscale policies if throughput changes.

alexa: thanks y'all. opening PRs now.

mike: :thumbsup:
